claims.statement: GitHub review-related webhook deliveries enter POST /webhooks/github, which verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC before parsing JSON, ignores unsupported events/actions, and schedules accepted handlers as FastAPI background tasks.

Automatic first reviews and push watch evaluation are gated by enabled-review-repository membership; the membership read intentionally fails soft, treating an unavailable store as not opted in rather than failing the webhook.
process_github_pr_ready skips automatic review of a draft unless the PR author's effective review_draft_prs setting is enabled.

An explicit PR review request reaches trigger_pr_review_from_ref, which fetches PR metadata, creates/addresses the reviewer thread, persists PR metadata with watch=True and head SHA, posts an in-progress comment, and dispatches the reviewer graph.

Every review of a PR uses reviewer_thread_id(owner, repo, pr_number), a UUIDv5 over '{owner}/{repo}/pr/{pr_number}/reviewer'; this cross-process derivation is a persisted routing contract whose change would orphan live reviewer threads.
Reviewer dispatches use assistant_id='reviewer', mapped to agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent, and store the dispatched run ID on reviewer-thread metadata.
A PR's evolving findings are persisted in metadata on its canonical reviewer thread, whose metadata is durable across sandbox eviction and queryable through the LangGraph SDK.
Every persisted finding read is normalized by coerce_finding: legacy singular GitHub identities and nested surface data are folded into canonical identity lists and surface_state.

Finding writes use a per-thread locked read-modify-write layer: mutate_findings persists only changes, replace_findings merges snapshots by finding ID, and append_finding de-duplicates fingerprints among open findings.
When reviewer-thread finding storage is absent, the storage layer raises ReviewerThreadMissingError and tools return a structured thread_not_found do-not-retry result.

add_finding enforces in-diff anchoring using file/side-specific line sets; invalid ranges return success:false and in_diff:false with a do-not-retry message, while file-level findings are stored but cannot render as inline comments.
add_finding requires a non-default generated title, validates severity/confidence/side and range order, and drops suggestions over the four-line MAX_SUGGESTION_LINES cap while retaining the finding.

Publication selection accepts open findings at or above a default medium threshold, orders low < medium < high < critical with stable severity/file/line sorting, caps at six, and does not use confidence as a gate.

publish_review submits eligible findings as one GitHub PR Review with inline path/line/side comments containing an Open SWE marker and optional suggestion; re-reviews restrict publication to unpublished findings first seen at the live head.

publish_review prefers the live head SHA from reviewer-thread metadata over frozen run configuration, then records the GitHub review and comment identities before later reconciliation backfills thread identities.

publish_review handles unresolved-anchor 422s by pruning identifiable bad findings and retrying once; an already-reviewed empty re-review skips a new summary while resolving threads and advancing state; eval mode is dry-run, and only an unflagged numeric review_id proves GitHub publication.
PR lifecycle handlers set reviewer watch true on reopen, false on close, and false on conversion to draft only when effective draft reviews are disabled.

Push re-review requires an opted-in watched reviewer thread for an open PR whose head changed; when its diff is unchanged it advances last_reviewed_sha and creates then completes a visible current-head 'No new changes to review' check without a reviewer run.

A changed-diff push reconciles current GitHub threads, refreshes reviewer metadata, creates a new check, and dispatches re_review=True with net-new reconciliation instructions; ready_for_review also skips a duplicate run when the head equals last_reviewed_sha.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads backfills finding publication identities, records the latest non-bot reply as a needs-reassessment interaction, and marks an open finding resolved only when all matching GitHub threads are resolved, persisting only on change.

A non-bot reply to an Open SWE review comment is reconciled and matched to its finding, recorded as a needs-reassessment FindingInteraction, then dispatched to the reviewer graph with reviewer_event='finding_reply'.

Review dispatch creates and stores an Open SWE Review check run; settlement clears its ID only after a successful PATCH and otherwise stores review_check_pending_result for a later retry with the intended conclusion.
If a reviewer exits without publishing, after-agent middleware settles its remaining review check as neutral; if a pending completion result exists, it retries that actual result instead.

The reviewer test suite covers auto-review gating, watch short circuits, bounded diff materialization and range semantics, finding storage/tools, publishing, and reconciliation, with additional graph, API/chat, grouping, outcomes, trace-context, and style tests.

The reviewer graph prepares a replaceable sandbox checkout at the PR head before model use, materializes a first-review merge-base diff or re-review incremental diff, and provides a review-specific read-only tool set rather than coding mutation tools.

Reviewer prompt construction treats PR title/body, existing review threads, and human replies as untrusted data by escaping/wrapping them and explicitly instructing the model not to follow embedded instructions.

Terminal finding resolution posts the required note as the complete reply to each unresolved associated GitHub thread and only records status resolved/dismissed after GitHub resolution succeeds; partial completion remains resolve_pending.
